reason: The cited evidence shows that a nanocrystalline glaze layer can yield low wear at 800 °C in a different alloy (E1) and that dynamic grain refinement can explain low friction in HEA (E2), but neither provides direct support for the key premises that oxide nanoparticles will induce this refinement in CoCrFeNi, that the glaze will persist from RT to 800 °C, or that the specific friction and wear targets will be met.
premises: Nanoparticles can act as nucleation sites for dynamic grain refinement at the sliding interface.
Dynamic grain refinement leads to a nanocrystalline glaze layer that reduces friction and wear.
A nanocrystalline glaze layer can be formed and maintained from RT to 800 °C in CoCrFeNi with oxide nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism (grain subdivision, suppressed dislocation plasticity) is operative in this alloy system.
The intervention will reduce friction to ~0.2–0.3 and wear by an order of magnitude across the full temperature range.
